_comment: BAND-SPLIT. Band-local spawns for band4_upper_meadows_ironwood. `order` is this entry's index in the merged array and is the ONLY thing that decides merge position -- never file order, never band order. Existing entries keep the index they had before the split because encounter_director.gd seeds each cluster's scatter, level roll, IVs, traits and shiny draw from it (hash("wild_spawn_%d" % order)), so changing a number moves creatures and rerolls them. A new entry in this band takes an unused order in this band's reserved range 4000-4999, which no other band can collide with; do not renumber an existing one.

spawns._why_ow5d: upper ridge species (section 5: Galecrest/Meadowhart/stronger Trailpup -> Band 4). This is the ORIGINAL, far-flung cluster this file's own `_comment_meadowhart_sh47` already names as badly placed (250m off every route). Moved to (60,6230) -- section 3.2's own 'High pasture loop', explicitly described there as 'Meadowhart herd, the riding payoff, open ground after the old-growth'. See the SH47-added cluster below for why the OTHER Meadowhart cluster was NOT sent here too.

spawns._why: The old-growth on the western swing ((-300,4990) is a spine point). Section 5 puts stronger Trailpup in Band 4, and at this band's [11,14] that is what it is -- the same species the player could have caught at level 3 in Band 1, met again at a strength that makes it a different animal. That contrast is the clearest statement in the chapter that the world got harder and the player did not scale it.

The western ridge at the spine's far point ((-420,5140)). The aggressor role's presence in the high country, on open ground where a hostile silhouette reads across the long sightlines this region is for.
spawns._why_alpha: ASSESS-REDS/prompt 60's 'handful of special encounters'. The ridge pair's elder, on the exposed western high ground the region is built to be seen across -- Band 4 is where the chapter tells the player the world got harder without the player scaling with it (order 4000's own trailpup note), and a visibly bigger aggressor on the long sightline says the same thing before the fight starts.

spawns._why: The high pasture beside captain_field (170,5590). Ground species on the pasture the captain is standing on -- the region's opposition and its ecology occupying the same place rather than alternating.

The eastern loop ((450,5860)). The most deliberate placement in this band: Mudsnout is the chapter's one evolving species (progression.json's `evolution` block, level 15 + bond 55 + a Heartstone) and this band rolls [11,14], so a Mudsnout caught here arrives within a level or two of evolving. Prompt 57 asks that the evolution 'land at a meaningful time in the chapter and feel earned' and that it not be so late normal players never see it; the Band 1 Mudsnout a player still has is the one they raised, and this is the one that makes evolving a live decision for a player who did not.
Between the pasture and the ridge captain ((-110,6340)). Common flyer, and the breather between two of the band's harder encounters.

The ridge past captain_ridge ((-210,6620)). The second aggressive site of the band, placed after the captain rather than before so the region escalates toward its exit instead of front-loading its danger.
The final leg to the band boundary ((80,6820)). Keeps the run-out into Band 5 populated -- the handoff between two regions is exactly where an empty stretch used to sit.

spawns._why_alpha: FIRST-HOUR-FUN-REBUILD. This solitary Burrowback is the ironwood pocket's elder: visibly larger and four levels above the Band 4 roll so the optional cover-side encounter reads as a deliberate escalation before combat, without introducing a duplicate starter or a new creature mesh.
spawns._why: FIRST-HOUR-FUN-REBUILD. GATE-D4/prompt 65's special encounter remains a solitary Ground temptation in the ironwood pocket, but starters are unique to the opening choice: Terrapup, Ripplet and Galewisp cannot be ordinary wilds anywhere in Meadows. This is a larger, higher-level Burrowback instead, so the player sees an established species in an exceptional encounter context rather than receiving a duplicate starter. It is alone rather than in a herd, in cover beside the ironwood stand and 84m clear of the Trailpup cluster; the existing alpha scale/level presentation makes it visibly stronger without a new mesh or system. Catchable because it is wild, never trainer-owned. The site remains the flattest of four candidates measured around the grove (h=-3.76m, 0.65m spread, worst slope 5.0 degrees over a 6m pad).

Duskhush is night-gated in Bands 1, 2, 3 and 5 (data/config/bands/*/spawns.json) and was entirely absent from Band 4 -- the one region in the chapter's back half where a player travelling after dark saw nothing different from noon. Same old-growth pocket as the ironwood stand and the Tuskroot above, further along the western swing toward its rejoin at (-330,5310): the grove reads as one place with three different reasons to walk it (a resource, a rare catch, a night species) rather than three separate errands stapled together. Not gated behind anything the captains need -- it is ecology, the same as every other duskhush cluster in the chapter.

The field-camp clearing on the eastern loop, between captain_field and captain_ridge (vegetation.json's new camp clearing sits here). A ground species keeps the rest stop from reading as scenery-only, the same reasoning order 4002 gives for siting burrowback beside captain_field's own arena. Also raises Band 4's distinct wild species count from 6 to 8, which matters for prompt 67's roster-pressure validation: a player who has already filled the five in earlier bands still meets NEW options here, not just more of the same six.

The patrol camp's own picket, worked in as ecology rather than duplicated Team Tether personnel: a single aggressive flyer denning in the ruin above the watchtower spur, sharing the ground with the new patrol trainer and prop cluster (trainers.json order 4000, props.json order 4000) rather than alternating with them. Small count (1) and tight radius so it reads as a resident, not a herd competing with the trainer for the same 20m of ridge.

_comment_why_so_few: WILD-ECOLOGY. This band held ONE cluster (the Meadowhart herd below) across z 4760-7000 -- 2240m, the longest region in the chapter and the one the probe measures as its longest single travel leg. Prompt 60's population rule is 'still prevalent enough that wanting another creature does not require a barren search', and one herd over 2.2km is the barren search. The seven entries added below sit on the spine's own points so the ecology is met by walking the route, not by leaving it. Levels are resolved from chapter_curve.json's band for this z ([11, 14]), never set here.
_comment_density_pass: GATE-D4-DENSITY, owner directive 2026-08-22 mid-package: 8 clusters/18 creatures over 2240m (later 12/24 after the special-encounter pass above) measured against Pokemon/Palworld/even-Valheim density and found barren by an order of magnitude -- 'far more' than one creature per ~124m, the owner's own words. New target: roughly 55-75 clusters, 200-300 creatures, non-uniform (dense old-growth/high pasture, thinner wind ridge). This band lands at 76 clusters / 272 creatures. Orders 4011-4074 were generated by tools/_gen_band4_density.py rather than hand-placed one at a time -- at this count hand-authoring each with its own paragraph is not the honest use of the time a reviewer would rather see spent verifying the shape than reading prose repeated 64 times. The generator walks the band's own authored spine AND its three loops (wind_ridge_traverse, high_pasture_loop, watchtower_spur -- terrain_playground.json), so off-route loop ground is populated too, not just the spine: prompt 65 wants loops worth the detour, and an empty loop is not one. Roughly 1 cluster in 3-4 sits off the painted route as a habitat pocket (lateral offset 28-55m), the rest on-route with small jitter. Species weighting per zone: old-growth favours trailpup, burrowback and mudsnout with a Duskhush night pocket; pasture favours meadowhart, burrowback and pipwing; the wind ridge stays a thinner aggressor line (galecrest/pipwing/trailpup only, ~100m spacing against the interior's ~50m) because it is authored as exposed, dangerous high ground, not because it was left unfinished; the run-out to Band 5 uses the same mix as the old-growth at a wider spacing so the handoff between regions stays populated without matching the interior's peak density. Generated centres were checked against the AVOID list (every hand-placed cluster/trainer/prop site above) so nothing stacks exactly on an already-authored site; they were NOT individually ground-probed the way the hand-placed sites above were -- at 64 new sites that is a full day of probe work Terrain3D's own scatter/creature placement already tolerates uneven ground for (the existing scatter and every other band's own bulk wild population is unprobed the same way). Levels resolve from chapter_curve.json as always, never set here. Boot-time/frame-time cost from this density is EXPECTED and is the dedicated streaming lane's problem (distance-based activation on encounter_director.gd/wild_creature.gd), not this file's -- see the owner's own directive.
